newsitem.title: UK: UK acts on monopolies report on film distribution.
newsitem.headline: UK acts on monopolies report on film distribution.

text.p: The government announced on Monday it was to restrict the minimum periods which distributors can insist on cinemas showing their films for.

Corporate Affairs Minister John Taylor said he had laid an order before Parliament, under which minimum exhibition periods would be a maximum of two weeks if the film was a new release and one week if not.
The order is due to come into force on March 1 next year.
"Cinemas have often been required by distributors to show a film for longer than they thought was justified. This Order will redress the balance," Taylor said in a statement.
The government move implements recommendations contained in a Monopolies and Mergers Commission report published in 1994.
The report found there was a complex monopoly situation involving leading film distributors and cinema chains.
It said that lengthy minimum exhibition periods, in some cases in excess of four weeks, were against the public interest.
